result:
`bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (3 tests, 0 fail).

The endpoint's code was all present but orphaned: `routes/admin.ts` exported `registerAdminRoutes`, and nothing ever called it, so `/admin/posts` was never added to the router — hence the 404 for guests and signed-in users alike. I fixed it in `routes/web.ts:7` by importing `registerAdminRoutes` from `./admin.js` and invoking it at `routes/web.ts:22`, right after `registerAuthRoutes(router)` and before the `/posts` group, so it receives the same router that carries the `auth`/`guest` middleware aliases — that gives the admin group's `router.middleware('auth')` the `requireAuthenticated({ redirectTo: '/login' })` behaviour every other signed-in-only page uses, and keeps it clear of the `/posts/:id` matching. `AdminPostController` and its route definition are untouched. I then ran `bun run codegen`, which picked the route up into `.guren/routes.gen.ts` (`admin.posts.index` → `GET /admin/posts`, plus the `routes.admin.posts.index()` helper), `.guren/api-client.gen.ts`, and `types/generated/routes.d.ts`. Finally I added `tests/AdminPostController.test.ts`, which boots the real app via `TestApp` and asserts a guest `GET /admin/posts` redirects to `/login` rather than 404ing — mirroring the existing starter tests, which stay database-free.
